assets.observation: Four visible curled fingers wrap the shaft from the left, with a thumb crossing from the right near the top of the fist. Handle passes through the fist and emerges below; a clear closed grip supports the upright microphone. Continuous hand and bent forearm; no visible wrist reversal.

Thumb braces the near/right base while finger pads curl from the left; the short top pad is occluded by the base rather than visibly detached. Lower fingers/palm support the black plinth from below as well as bracing it laterally. Continuous bent forearm and palm, with no gap at the prop contact.

Thumb braces the right wall of the pot; front fingertips curl upward from a continuous palm underneath. Broad palm shelf supports the pot base directly, with visible contact and a plausible weight path to the wrist. Hand, wrist, and forearm are continuous. No cut or disconnection is visible in source or native output.

The thumb opposes the curled fingertips around the stem bundle. Stems pass through the closed grip and continue below the hand; the bouquet load is carried at the grip. Wrist flows into the forearm without a reversal.
The pronated hand closes over the top of the handle, with flexed fingers dropping across it. The bag hangs below that contact and the wrist connects continuously to the forearm.
The upper thumb opposes a finger at the handle opening, with curled fingers supporting below. The porcelain cup extends outward from the held handle and the wrist stays continuous.

The right hand is supinated beneath the near palette edge; curled fingertips support the underside while the thumb presses over the near rim. The brush lies on the board. The thumb, palm and wrist connect coherently.
assets.releaseNote: Thinner supporting fingers are accepted as a plausible pose/foreshortening. No source or palm-width calibration change is selected.

assets.observation: The five-digit resting hand is the mirrored counterpart of gesture/rest. Its thumb is medial and the back of the hand faces the viewer; the forearm reaches the correct viewer-left socket.
Back of the left hand faces the viewer. Four relaxed long fingers and a medial thumb form five digits; the wrist and forearm are continuous.
Palm faces the viewer; medial thumb and four spread fingers are distinct. Palm creases and thumb pad agree with the left-hand orientation.

Back-of-left-hand interpretation is coherent: thumb extends outward, little finger inward, with three folded middle digits. The apparent reversal relative to palm-facing gestures is not an extra or wrong-side thumb.
The thumb rises from the medial side, with four folded fingers visible along the other side. Wrist bend and palm mass remain continuous.
Two extended fingers, two folded fingers and a thumb across them are readable. Thumb placement and palm orientation match the left arm.
The index is foreshortened toward the viewer. Thumb and curled fingers surround its base without passing through it; side occlusion accounts for the compact fist.
Index and little finger are extended; the middle and ring fingers fold under the thumb. Five-digit topology and left-palm orientation are coherent.
Thumb and index meet in a closed ring while three other fingers extend. The ring is made from two opposed fingertips, not a fused extra digit.
Four curled fingers and an outside thumb are visible. The thumb wraps across the folded fingers rather than being trapped through them.
Four fingers are aligned toward the brow and the thumb folds under the palm. Elbow, forearm and wrist lead naturally to the forehead contact.
Bent elbow and forearm lead to a rotated closed fist; partly hidden digits are consistent with that oblique view. Large biceps are an intentional cartoon exaggeration, not a disconnected joint.
Thumb and index cross near their tips while the other three fingers curl into the palm. Their paths are readable and the wrist is continuous.
The left palm is supinated, with a raised medial thumb and four fingers extending outward. Palm, thumb pad and wrist direction agree.
Back of the left hand faces outward, with thumb above the four fingers. Fingers rest over the body and the bent arm connects at the wrist without reversal.
